expectations.text: Cloud services (M365, AWS) are IN scope and cannot be excluded — with the shared-responsibility split by SaaS/IaaS and the customer always owning user access control/MFA enablement
expectations.evidence: 'cloud services... cannot be excluded from scope'; 'M365 (SaaS)... you always own user access control'; 'AWS (IaaS): you own... access control'

expectations.text: BYOD phones accessing organisational data/email are IN scope (out only if used solely for calls/texts/MFA apps)
expectations.evidence: 'if a device accesses organisational data or services... it's in scope'; 'only BYOD carve-out is a device used solely for native phone calls/SMS or purely as an MFA authenticator app'

expectations.text: Home working devices are in scope; home ISP routers are OUT of scope with the device's software firewall as the boundary; organisation-supplied home routers are in; corporate VPN moves the boundary to the corporate/virtual/cloud firewall
expectations.evidence: 'home ISP routers are explicitly OUT of scope... boundary control becomes the software firewall'; 'If you supply staff with your own routers... in scope'; VPN 'boundary shifts... to that corporate/virtual firewall'

expectations.text: States that MFA is mandatory on all cloud services (and an auto-fail if missing where available)
expectations.evidence: 'Missing MFA on a cloud service that supports it is an automatic-fail condition under Danzell'

expectations.text: Notes scope-declaration mechanics under the current requirements: whole-organisation preferred, sub-sets need firewall/VLAN segregation and justified exclusions, and whole-org scope is required for the bundled insurance
expectations.evidence: Recommends whole-org scope but never states sub-set firewall/VLAN segregation requirements or that whole-org scope is required for the bundled insurance
